issues.title: False derivative term in the continuous uniqueness proof
issues.failure_explanation: The proof treats Re(i(∂tψ,e^{-·/T}∂tψ)) as the positive weighted derivative norm, although the inner product is real and that real part is zero. Removing the term proves uniqueness for μ≠0; for μ=0 the homogeneous equation directly gives ∂tψ=0.
issues.overall_effect: The stated continuous uniqueness result is true, but its printed proof contains a false equality and does not establish the μ=0 case after the equality is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the homogeneous uniqueness proof, replace the false derivative-norm term by the correct identity 0 = μ[(1/(2T))∫₀ᵀ|ψ(s)|²e^{-s/T}ds + (1/(2e))|ψ(T)|²], since the real part of i(∂ₜψ,e^{-·/T}∂ₜψ) is zero. For μ≠0 this gives ψ≡0; for μ=0, the homogeneous equation directly implies ∂ₜψ=0, and ψ(0)=0 then gives ψ≡0.
issues.why_classification: The false equality is used as a proof step, so this is not a transcription-only typo. Nevertheless, one corrected calculation and a routine μ=0 case split recover the proposition at its full stated strength without a new lemma or any mathematical loss.

issues.title: Symbol polynomial omits the coefficients of the matrix family
issues.failure_explanation: Equation (21) defines the matrix family as iB−ρC. Because taking the symbol polynomial is linear, equation (25) must retain the factor i and the minus sign. The printed formula represents a different matrix family.
issues.overall_effect: The labeled symbol formula contradicts the defining matrix equation. The later unit-circle expression already uses the intended coefficients, so the demonstrated defect is a local transcription inconsistency rather than a separate loss of the stability range.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace equation (25) by q^{K^p(ρ)}(z) = i q^{B^p}(z) − ρ q^{C^p}(z). No downstream argument needs alteration because the later unit-circle expression already uses these coefficients.
issues.why_classification: The defining identity K^p(ρ)=iB^p−ρC^p and linearity of the symbol uniquely force the missing factor and sign. The surrounding analysis uses the corrected expression, so the defect is a local transcription error rather than a failed inference.

issues.title: Outer-codiagonal hypothesis checked only for positive parameters

failure_location.quote: provided that we show the entries of the two outer codiagonals (the $(-p-1)^{\text{th}}$ and the $(p-1)^{\text{th}}$) of $\K_n^p(\rho)$ are nonzero for all $\rho>0$ and $p \in \N$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which shows that, for all $ p \in \mathbb{N} $, the entries of these codiagonals in both $ \bC_n^p $ and $ \B_n^p $ are nonzero.

issues.failure_explanation: The weak-conditioning consequence in Proposition 3.9 uses Theorem 3.9 for the family indexed by real ρ, but Step 2 verifies its outer-codiagonal hypothesis only for ρ>0. Since B and C are real and an outer entry of B is nonzero, the imaginary part of iB−ρC is nonzero for every real ρ; that all-real argument is absent from the old invocation.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 3.9's weak-conditioning consequence is not justified outside the positive-ρ range, and the all-real conclusion of Theorem 3.13 inherits this unmet-hypothesis gap. The later wave theorem only uses a positive square root and is not dependent on this missing branch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the outer-codiagonal check to every real ρ: each relevant entry has the form ib−ρc with b,c real and b≠0 by the cited result, so its imaginary part is b and cannot vanish for any ρ∈R. State this before invoking Theorem 3.9, thereby closing the same hypothesis check for the affected all-real conclusion in Theorem 3.13.
issues.why_classification: The old invocation has a genuine quantifier and dependency gap, but the missing verification is a one-line real/imaginary-part argument using facts already present in the source. It preserves the full statements and requires no nontrivial new result.

issues.title: Unsupported negative-parameter branch of the main stability theorem

failure_location.quote: Then, for all~$p \in \N$ and~$\rho \in \R$, the family of matrices~$\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:21} is weakly well-conditioned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For~$\rho>0$ and~$p \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $K_p(\theta,\rho)$ has exactly 2 simple zeros

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims weak conditioning for all real ρ, but the only old zero-count result used to obtain it, Proposition 3.12, assumes ρ>0. Proposition 3.9 is conditional on having the required unit-circle zeros and therefore does not supply the missing negative-ρ branch.
issues.overall_effect: The negative-ρ part of Theorem 3.13 is not established. The later wave theorem uses μs=√μw>0, so it needs only the already covered positive branch and is not a dependent formal result of this defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the all-real theorem and supplement the established positive-parameter branch as follows. For every r>0, K_n^p(−r)=−overline{K_n^p(r)}, so the positive and negative families have identical nonsingularity and condition numbers. At ρ=0, K_n^p(0)=iB_n^p, and the weak conditioning of the B-family is already available from the cited result. These observations establish the theorem for all ρ∈R without extending the zero-count proof.
issues.why_classification: The omitted negative branch is a real support gap in a substantive parameter regime, so it is not a typo. However, an exact conjugation symmetry transfers the full positive-branch guarantee locally, and the zero case is already known; thus no weakening, new architecture, or nontrivial lemma is needed.

issues.title: Continuous wave-state ordering mismatches the discrete formulation

failure_location.quote:
The discrete variational formulation 
of~\eqref{eq:29} proposed in~\cite{FerrariFraschiniLoliPerugia2024} reads:

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that (30) is the discrete variational formulation of (29). The old system has ∂tv=u and ∂tu+μwv=f, whose integration-by-parts formulation would start with derivatives of v and then u. Equation (30) instead starts with derivatives of u and couples v, so it discretizes the system obtained by exchanging u and v. The mismatch concerns the claimed continuous-to-discrete interface, not the algebraic formulation (30) itself.
issues.overall_effect: The state variables in the continuous wave model are misidentified relative to the discrete method. Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.2 analyze the discrete block system and remain unaffected after relabeling.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Exchange the labels u and v in the continuous system (29), writing ∂ₜu−v=0 and ∂ₜv+μ_wu=f, or equivalently state explicitly that the variables in (30) use the reverse state ordering. The zero initial data and all later analysis of (30) remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The two continuous systems differ only by names assigned to the two state components, and equation (30) together with the subsequent block formulation uniquely fixes the intended ordering. Correcting that ordering repairs no mathematical inference or construction and changes no guarantee.

issues.title: Missing uniqueness-hypothesis transfer in the wave-stability theorem

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{th:313} guarantees the stability of the variational formulation~\eqref{eq:10}

issues.failure_explanation: The invoked Theorem 3.13 is conditional on Assumption 3.4, whereas Theorem 4.2 states only uniqueness of the wave formulation. Although the block matrices in (33) make the implication recoverable, the proof invokes Theorem 3.13 before proving that wave uniqueness yields Schrödinger uniqueness for every real μs.
issues.overall_effect: The wave-stability conclusion has an omitted prerequisite argument, but its stated hypothesis is sufficient once the Schur-complement transfer is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Before invoking Theorem 3.13, derive its uniqueness assumption from the wave hypothesis. Since B_h^p is invertible, for μ_s≠0 set μ_w=μ_s²; invertibility of the wave block matrix implies invertibility of the Schur complement B_h^p+μ_s²C_h^p(B_h^p)^{-1}C_h^p, which is also the Schur complement of the Schrödinger real block matrix. Hence the Schrödinger formulation is unique for μ_s≠0, while μ_s=0 follows directly from invertibility of B_h^p. Theorem 3.13 may then be applied as written.
issues.why_classification: The theorem omits a prerequisite implication, but it follows by a short, standard Schur-complement argument using matrices already displayed in the proof. This local addition preserves the wave theorem's original hypothesis and conclusion without substantive loss.

issues.title: Incorrect Schur-transformed operator in Algorithm 1
issues.failure_explanation: Writing D=(iB)^{-1}C and QᴴDQ=R, left preconditioning (35) by (iB)^{-1} and applying the Schur basis produces I⊗M+R⊗A. The old Step 4 attaches M to R^{-1}, which is neither this transformed operator nor generally algebraically equivalent to it.
issues.overall_effect: Step 4 generally solves a different block system, so the stated procedure does not implement the advertised global solve.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let D=(iB_{h_t}^p)^{-1}C_{h_t}^p and Q^HDQ=R. Left preconditioning and the Schur change of basis give (I⊗M+R⊗A)Z=(Q^H⊗I)((iB)^{-1}⊗I)F with Z=(Q^H⊗I)Ψ, followed by Ψ=(Q⊗I)Z. Replace Step 4 by this transformed solve, remove the unnecessary use of R^{-1}, and implement the surrounding right-hand-side and inverse-basis transformations consistently with this identity.
issues.why_classification: The old step is an actual algebraic error in the executable construction, so it is not merely typographical. A short standard Kronecker-product derivation supplies a local correction that retains the same Bartels–Stewart architecture, block-triangular solve, complexity, and exact-solve guarantee.
